description: Centralized Python virtual environment manager — pyenv-style workflow powered by uv. Written in Rust.
rules: scuv is installed via `cargo install scoop-uv`. The binary name is `scuv` (renamed from `scoop` in v0.15.0 to coexist with scoop.sh), the crate name is `scoop-uv`.
Configuration file is at ~/.scuv/config.json (JSON format, NOT TOML). Never reference ~/.config/scuv/config.toml.
Virtual environments are stored centrally in ~/.scuv/virtualenvs/.
Shell integration uses the eval pattern (like pyenv): `eval "$(scuv init zsh)"`.
Supported shells: bash, zsh, fish, powershell.
Supported languages: en, ko, ja, pt-BR, es. Set via `scuv lang <code>` or SCUV_LANG env var.
Version file priority: SCUV_VERSION env > .scuv-version (local + parent walk) > ~/.scuv/version (global).
To set a specific Python version globally, create an environment with that version, then run `scuv use <env> --global`.
`scuv use --global` writes an environment name to ~/.scuv/version, not a raw Python version string.
To create a new environment with an exact Python version (for example 3.9.5), use `scuv install 3.9.5` then `scuv create <name> 3.9.5`.
Verify environment Python with `scuv info <name>`. If version resolution fails, inspect `uv python list` and `scuv list --pythons`.
To remove a Python version and all associated environments, use `scuv uninstall <version> --cascade` (add `--force` for non-interactive use).
Without `--cascade`, uninstalling Python does not delete dependent environments and they may become broken; verify cleanup with `scuv list --pythons` and `scuv doctor`.
For temporary auto-activation disable without global impact, use `export SCUV_NO_AUTO=1` in the current shell and `unset SCUV_NO_AUTO` when done.
For project-specific behavior, use local `.scuv-version` via `scuv use <env>` or `scuv use system`; for terminal-only override use `scuv shell <env|system>` and `scuv shell --unset`.
Once an environment is active, install dependencies from requirements file with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
For non-root dependency files, use `pip install -r path/to/requirements.txt`; verify installed packages with `pip list`.
To inspect managed versions and associations: `scuv list --pythons` (versions), `scuv list` (envs), and `scuv list --python-version <VERSION>` (envs for one version).
Use `--json` for machine-readable output and `--bare` for script-friendly output when listing versions or environments.

If required Python is unavailable in default sources, integrate custom interpreters via `scuv create <env> --python-path /path/to/python` or add interpreter to PATH then run `scuv create <env> <version>`.
Verify custom integration using `uv python list`, `scuv info <env>`, and `scuv doctor -v`; custom interpreter path is stored in `.scoop-metadata.json` (`python_path`).
.python-version is NOT supported. Use .scuv-version for version pinning.
Environment names must match ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$ (max 64 chars, must start with letter).
Most commands support --json for machine-readable output.
MSRV is 1.89 (required by serde-saphyr 1.2, via rust-i18n; Edition 2024's own floor is 1.85). The MSRV is dependency-driven — it rises only when a dependency requires it.
Project manifest file is .scuv.toml (parent-walk discovery from cwd). Defines [environment].python and [packages].default + named groups; reconcile the active env with the manifest via `scuv sync`.
To run a one-off command in an env without activating it, use `scuv run <env> -- <cmd>` (e.g. `scuv run myproject -- pytest tests/`). The `--` separator is required before the command.
To inspect current state use `scuv status` (Active/Configured/System/None) and `scuv which <exe>` (resolves an executable inside the active env).

For collaboration, snapshot an env with `scuv export <name> > env.json` (schema v1) and restore with `scuv import env.json --name <new>`. To duplicate locally, use `scuv clone <src> <dst>` (add `--no-packages` for a skeleton).
Lazy Python install: `scuv create <name> <version> --install-python` installs the requested Python via uv if missing, then creates the env.
`scuv migrate all` runs in parallel via rayon; `--dry-run` and single-env (`migrate @env`) stay sequential.
To free disk space from the uv download/wheel cache, run `scuv prune` (thin wrapper around `uv cache prune`).

To clean up orphan virtualenvs (missing metadata or broken Python), run `scuv gc` (default is preview/dry-run). Pass `-y`/`--yes` to actually remove. `--aggressive` also flags uv-managed Python versions that no environment references.

To diagnose env health, run `scuv verify [NAME]`. Runs 6 checks per env (metadata, python binary, pyvenv.cfg, activate script, python executes, .scuv.toml drift). Default always exits 0; pass `--strict` to exit 1 on any issue for CI gates. Use `verify` for per-env diagnosis, `doctor` for system-level, `gc` to remove orphans.
To generate man pages, use `scuv man` (stdout, pipe to `man -l -`) or `scuv man <DIR>` (writes `scuv.1` + `scuv-<sub>.1` files for distro packagers).
For complete LLM reference, see llms-full.txt in the repository root.
